title: Verisma Reviews 2026
summary: Verisma reviews for 2026: what Verisma offers attorneys as requesters, its pricing litigation history, and how Codes Health compares for plaintiff firms.
body_markdown:
When legal teams search for "Verisma reviews," they're often looking for a medical record retrieval service built for plaintiff law firms. Verisma Systems is mainly a Release of Information (ROI) and disclosure management company whose core platform is built for healthcare providers and health plans. Attorneys can use Verisma's requester tools to submit, track, pay for, and receive records from participating healthcare organizations, but Verisma doesn't publicly position its core offering as an end-to-end litigation retrieval and analysis platform for plaintiff firms. That distinction matters for personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice practices choosing a solution for their caseloads. Platforms like[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) work from the law firm's side, handling outbound record retrieval across every provider in a case along with AI-powered case analysis.


This review looks at Verisma's capabilities, target market, strengths, and limitations to help you decide whether it fits your workflow, or whether a legal-focused retrieval and analysis platform is the better fit.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


**Verisma's core platform serves providers and health plans.** Attorneys can use its requester tools to submit, track, pay for, and receive records from participating healthcare organizations, but it isn't positioned as an end-to-end litigation platform.


-


**Different markets, different strengths.** Verisma focuses on provider-side ROI management, while Codes Health specializes in legal-side retrieval and AI case analysis.


-


**Law firms need retrieval across every provider in a case.** Verisma's requester tools cover its participating organizations, and its Retrieval IQ service is marketed to health plans and healthcare organizations rather than plaintiff firms.


-


**AI capabilities differ by purpose.** Verisma's AI supports ROI intake, retrieval, and compliance review, while Codes Health uses purpose-built AI to flag potential breaches of care, pre-existing conditions, and future medical expenses for attorney review.


-


**Pricing models differ.** Plaintiffs in one case alleged a[$0.75 per page](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/ca2/22-2928/22-2928-2024-01-29.html) rate regardless of production costs, though the court ultimately ruled for the defendants. Codes Health uses flat fee pricing with no per-page charges.


-


**Complete records in a couple of weeks.** Codes Health works toward complete medical records in a couple of weeks, with completeness verified before delivery.


## **Understanding Medical Records Requests: A Look at Verisma's Role**


Medical records requests in legal workflows follow a specific path: the law firm identifies providers, submits authorizations, and pursues records until the full set arrives. Verisma sits mostly on the other side of that exchange. It helps healthcare providers receive, validate, and fulfill incoming requests, and it gives requesters, including attorneys, tools to interact with participating organizations.


### **Verisma's Approach to Health Information Management**


Verisma positions itself as an enterprise ROI platform. The company reports supporting 20,000+ client sites and processing 63.3 million records monthly. Its core functions include:


-


Request intake management for hospitals and health systems


-


Disclosure compliance tracking and audit trails


-


Authorization validation from the provider perspective


-


HIPAA-compliant response workflows


For attorneys, Verisma offers a Requestor Support Center and an attorney version of its Request App, which let law firms submit requests digitally, check status, pay, and download records from participating healthcare organizations. Verisma markets the app as a way to shorten request turnaround compared with paper-driven workflows.


That can streamline requests sent to Verisma's client organizations. Verisma's public materials, however, don't show the same end-to-end, multi-provider litigation retrieval and completeness workflow Codes Health offers.


### **Streamlining Medical Record Requests for Providers**


For healthcare HIM departments, Verisma offers:


-


Centralized request intake across multiple facilities


-


Automated routing based on request type


-


Compliance documentation for audits


-


An Integration Engine that Verisma says works across 7,000+ EHR and health data source connections


These capabilities mainly address provider needs. Law firms looking for retrieval across unrelated providers, missing record detection, or case-critical medical insights will want to look at how each vendor handles those specific workflows.


## **Health Information Management: Verisma's Offerings and the Future with AI**


Verisma has operated for more than 24 years in the health information management space. In March 2025, the company announced an AI suite integrating Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service into its workflows.


### **The Evolving Role of HIM in Healthcare**


Modern health information management increasingly relies on technology to handle volume. Verisma's AI suite covers areas such as:


-


AI-enabled request intake


-


Automated categorization and extraction


-


RPA and API-supported retrieval


-


Human-in-the-loop review and technology-assisted review


-


LLM-powered requester status support


These tools focus on ROI and health information management workflows. Verisma's current public materials don't advertise extracting legal case insights or generating litigation-ready chronologies for plaintiff firms.


### **Where Legal AI Differs**


AI built for provider compliance and ROI processing serves a different purpose than AI built for plaintiff litigation.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) uses AI purpose-built for medical record analysis in legal contexts, flagging for attorney review:


-


Potential breaches in care standards


-


Pre-existing conditions affecting case value


-


Missed appointments and treatment gaps


-


Future medical expenses documented in records


-


Provider inconsistencies relevant to litigation strategy


That matters because legal teams need insights that shape case strategy, not just efficient request processing.


## **Viewing Medical Records Online: How Verisma and Other Solutions Facilitate Access**


Patient and requester access through a provider's ROI vendor works differently from litigation retrieval. Verisma helps participating organizations release records to patients and requesters, while law firms often need records from many facilities that use different vendors and systems.


### **Challenges in Online Record Retrieval for Legal Teams**


When attorneys retrieve records, common obstacles include:


-


Multiple providers with different systems and requirements


-


Incomplete patient recollection of treatment history


-


Varying response times across facilities


-


Authorization rejections due to form errors


-


Limited visibility into retrieval status across providers


Verisma now offers active medical record retrieval through Retrieval IQ, which coordinates provider outreach, tracks received and outstanding records, quality-checks records, and identifies gaps for escalation. Its current public materials, however, position that service for health plans and healthcare organizations rather than plaintiff-law-firm litigation workflows.


### **Multi-Channel Active Retrieval**


Codes Health retrieves records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, and patient portals, while keeping up fax, email, and phone follow-up. This multi-channel approach is designed to get records from providers however they operate, with automated daily follow-ups until delivery.


## **The Intricacies of Release of Information: Verisma's Process vs. AI-Driven Efficiency**


Release of information workflows create friction for both providers and requesters. Verisma streamlines much of the provider side, while legal-focused platforms like Codes Health streamline the requester side.


### **Standardizing ROI Procedures**


Verisma's ROI platform helps healthcare organizations:


-


Validate incoming authorization forms


-


Track disclosure compliance


-


Maintain audit trails for regulatory review


-


Apply consistent fee structures


Verisma currently reports 99.99% release accuracy across its provider network, a metric that appears to change over time on its website.


### **Accelerating ROI with Technology**


For law firms, speed depends heavily on preventing errors before submission. Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force you to correct and resubmit. Common rejection triggers include:


-


Missing patient signatures


-


Unclear expiration dates


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive records (mental health, HIV, substance abuse)


-


Misspellings in patient names or facility names


-


Missing dates of service


A defective authorization can require correction and resubmission, delaying processing and, depending on the request type and jurisdiction, causing an applicable response period to begin again. For example, HIPAA's right of access generally gives covered entities 30 days to respond to an individual's request, with state variations, while attorney-authorized requests may follow different procedures.


[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) catches these errors before submission. The system automatically flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections. Codes Health reviews authorizations on the requester's side before submission, rather than relying solely on the receiving provider's ROI workflow to identify defects.


## **Exploring Medical Records Software: Verisma's Systems and Modern Alternatives**


Medical records software varies a lot based on who it's built for. Provider-focused systems like Verisma center on disclosure workflows, while legal-focused platforms center on retrieval and analysis.


### **Key Features of Medical Records Software for Legal Use**


Law firms evaluating medical records solutions should prioritize:


-


**Active retrieval capability:** Does the platform obtain records from every provider in a case, or mainly manage requests to its own client organizations?


-


**AI case analysis:** Can it identify legally relevant medical facts?


-


**Missing record detection:** Does it cross-reference patient history for completeness?


-


**Legal case chronologies:** Are records organized for litigation timelines?


-


**Authorization error checking:** Does it catch problems on your side before submission?


-


**Turnaround expectations:** What timeline can you expect for complete records?


Verisma addresses attorney request submission and tracking, but its current public materials don't advertise plaintiff-side case chronologies, breach-of-care analysis, future medical expense extraction, or other litigation-specific medical analysis.

Modern legal practice management increasingly demands integrated workflows. Since the July 13, 2026 partnership, Filevine users can submit, track, and receive Codes Health requests directly inside their case files. Codes Health can also build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume legal practices, keeping retrieval and analysis inside existing workflows rather than in separate portals.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, so the platform keeps evolving, improving, and becoming more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices.


## **HIPAA Compliance in Medical Record Retrieval: Adherence and Best Practices**


Both Verisma and legal retrieval platforms must maintain strict HIPAA compliance, but their obligations differ based on their roles in the information exchange.


### **Ensuring Data Security in Retrieval**


Verisma documents HITRUST r2 certification, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS/SSL encryption in transit, audit controls in its ROI workflow, and an internal AI and Data Governance Committee. HITRUST describes r2 as its highest-assurance core certification.


Codes Health operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform with Business Associate Agreements covering protected health information handling. The difference lies in purpose: Verisma helps providers release information compliantly, while Codes Health helps law firms receive and analyze information within regulatory frameworks.


## **Efficient Medical Record Retrieval: Comparing Verisma's Process to AI-Powered Speed**


Speed and completeness define retrieval success in litigation.


### **Reducing Retrieval Bottlenecks**


Retrieval timelines can stretch into months due to:


-


Manual follow-up processes


-


Provider response variability


-


Authorization errors requiring resubmission


-


No systematic completeness verification


-


Client involvement in gap identification


Speed alone doesn't solve this. Codes Health notes that competitors offering same-day retrieval often return only the records immediately available, which means clients get pulled in to track down the rest, and in Codes Health's experience that leads to churn. Codes Health works toward complete records in a couple of weeks, not months, through systematic multi-channel retrieval that doesn't depend on your clients chasing gaps. Automated daily follow-ups continue with every provider until records arrive.


### **The Impact of AI on Speed and Accuracy**


Verisma's Retrieval IQ is marketed for health plan programs such as HEDIS, Stars, and RADV, where the health plan retrieves records for quality and risk adjustment purposes. That's a different job than legal retrieval, where the attorney needs complete records for case development.


Codes Health's AI validates requests before submission to head off rejection cycles. Combined with Missing Record Review, which cross-references patient history to identify gaps before trial, the focus is on completeness, not just speed.


## **Beyond Retrieval: How AI Augments Medical Record Analysis for Legal Cases**


Record retrieval is only half the challenge. Turning thousands of pages into actionable legal insights is what shapes case strategy.


### **From Documents to Actionable Insights**


Verisma's current public product materials don't advertise litigation-focused medical case analysis or legal case chronology generation. Law firms need technology that extracts:


-


Diagnoses, treatments, and medical history


-


Treatment timelines and care patterns


-


Provider documentation inconsistencies


-


Pre-existing conditions affecting case value


-


Documented future medical needs and expenses


-


Potential breaches in care standards


Codes Health's insights extraction engine surfaces these facts for attorney review while generating automated case chronologies organized for litigation strategy. Patient encounters and bills are grouped by visit, exposing treatment gaps and documentation issues without manual review of every page.


### **AI's Role in Litigation Support**


Purpose-built legal AI differs from general-purpose platforms. General AI tools like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. Codes Health's platform is built to analyze medical records with high precision, combining AI processing with medical and legal expert verification so insights support, rather than replace, attorney judgment.


## **Historical Pricing Litigation**


Verisma's fees have been the subject of past litigation. In[McCracken v. Verisma Systems](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/ca2/22-2928/22-2928-2024-01-29.html) , plaintiffs alleged that Verisma charged a uniform $0.75 per page rate even where production costs were lower. In 2024, the Second Circuit affirmed judgment for the defendants, holding that the plaintiffs could not pursue the asserted claims based on New York's medical record fee statute.


Separately, Verisma and other defendants entered a reported settlement of approximately $4.9 million in the Wisconsin[Hammetter litigation](https://law.justia.com/cases/wisconsin/court-of-appeals/2021/2019ap002423.html) , which involved disputed certification and retrieval fees charged for records requested in connection with personal injury representation.


Codes Health uses transparent flat fee pricing without per-page charges. For law firms managing retrieval costs across large caseloads, predictable pricing makes case economics easier to plan.

Attorneys can use its requester tools to submit, track, pay for, and receive records from participating organizations, but Verisma doesn't publicly advertise litigation-focused retrieval and analysis for plaintiff firms.


### **How do AI platforms like Codes Health differ from provider-side ROI platforms?**


Provider-side platforms like Verisma focus on processing and releasing records for their client organizations. Codes Health combines active multi-channel retrieval across every provider in a case with AI-powered analysis that flags legally relevant insights such as potential breaches of care, pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps, and future medical expenses for attorney review.


### **What are the key HIPAA compliance considerations when using a medical record retrieval vendor?**


Law firms should verify that any retrieval vendor operates as a HIPAA-compliant platform with appropriate Business Associate Agreements. Key elements include encryption standards, audit trail capabilities, access controls, and documented security protocols. Both Verisma and Codes Health maintain HIPAA-compliant operations, and Verisma also documents HITRUST r2 certification.

Long retrieval timelines typically result from authorization errors requiring resubmission, provider response variability, manual follow-up, and no systematic completeness verification. A defective authorization can require correction and resubmission, and depending on the request type and jurisdiction, an applicable response period may begin again. AI-assisted validation before submission, combined with automated daily follow-up, can significantly reduce these delays.


### **Can Verisma help law firms with case chronologies or medical analysis?**


Verisma's current public product materials focus on provider-side disclosure management, requester tools, and health plan retrieval. They don't advertise legal case chronology generation, breach-of-care identification, or litigation-focused medical record analysis. Law firms needing these capabilities should look for a platform designed for legal workflows.
